commit_message:
HFE - RDB serialize also hash min expiration (For ROF flow) (#13391)

* Following this feature, Redis (ROF) may implement flow that allows hashes to be
  dumped directly from RDB to FLUSH without parsing. In this scenario, it is still
  essential to determine when to update hashes due to expired fields. By writing
  and reading the next minimum hash-field expiration before serializing objects
  to and from RDB, we can effectively track and expire hash fields without the need
  to parse the hash during loading.

    Before:
    #define RDB_TYPE_HASH_METADATA 22
    #define RDB_TYPE_HASH_LISTPACK_EX 23
    
    After:
    /* Hash with HFEs. Doesn't attach min TTL at start */
    #define RDB_TYPE_HASH_METADATA_PRE_GA 22      
    /* Hash LP with HFEs. Doesn't attach min TTL at start */
    #define RDB_TYPE_HASH_LISTPACK_EX_PRE_GA 23   
    /* Hash with HFEs. Attach min TTL at start */
    #define RDB_TYPE_HASH_METADATA 24             
    /* Hash LP with HFEs. Attach min TTL at start */
    #define RDB_TYPE_HASH_LISTPACK_EX 25          


* Manually test loading RDB file before the change and verify hash and its HFEs 
  is as expected.
* Added `subexpires` counter to `redis-check-rdb`

fix_commit.message: Fix short read of hfe key that causes exit() on replica (#14143)
fix_commit.author: Ozan Tezcan

findings.title: Short read of hash-field-expiration min-expire time wrongly treated as corruption, causing exit() on replica
findings.message: When loading RDB_TYPE_HASH_METADATA (and similarly RDB_TYPE_HASH_LISTPACK_EX) objects, rdbLoadObject() reads a serialized 'min expiration time' field via rdbLoadMillisecondTime() and then checks rioGetReadError(rdb) to detect a failed read. On failure it calls rdbReportCorruptRDB(), which invokes rdbReportError() with corruption_error=1. During diskless replication full sync, a transient/broken network connection to the master produces exactly this kind of short read (not actual data corruption), but because corruption_error is hard-coded to 1 via the CorruptRDB macro, rdbReportError() takes the 'In diskless loading, in case of corrupt file, log and exit' branch and falls through to exit(1), killing the replica process. The correct handling (as used elsewhere for genuine short reads over a socket) is to call rdbReportReadError(), which sets corruption_error=0 so rdbReportError() logs 'assuming connection error, resuming operation' and returns without exiting. This is purely a classification/logic bug: a recoverable network short-read condition is misclassified as a file-corruption condition, leading to replica self-termination (DoS) that is remotely triggerable by any master (or MITM on the replication link) that drops the connection at the right moment while streaming an HFE-enabled hash key.
findings.suggestion: Use rdbReportReadError() instead of rdbReportCorruptRDB() when a short/broken read of the min-expire time is detected via rioGetReadError(), for both the RDB_TYPE_HASH_METADATA and RDB_TYPE_HASH_LISTPACK_EX load paths, so that a dropped replication connection is treated as a recoverable connection error (log + resume) rather than unconditionally terminating the process via exit(1).

ground_truth.root_cause: The HFE min-expire-time RDB loading code added in commit dcf02298110 (#13391) reused rdbReportCorruptRDB() for a read-error check that can legitimately fire on a benign short read over a replication socket, instead of using rdbReportReadError() which is the designated helper for exactly this short-read/connection-drop scenario elsewhere in rdb.c. This mixes up the 'corrupted on-disk file' failure class with the 'broken network stream' failure class, both of which flow through the shared rdbReportError()/corruption_error parameter.
